clue.text: Booze from the East Indies

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone sources their drink from the spice islands of the East Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so it counts as a kind of booze.

clue.text: Put on and swear backwards, indeed

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for a deed

parts.note: an act is a deed

indicators.note: backwards says the word for swearing is read from right to left

parts.note: to eff is to swear, from the euphemism for the F-word

explanation.surface: Someone feigns things and curses in reverse, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word must be split as 'in deed' to read: the swearing reversed sits in the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect a manner is to put it on, to feign or pretend to it.

clue.text: Film a potty ballad about space women

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a child's potty

indicators.note: about has the song wrapped round the printer's space

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean ballad or song
an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

explanation.surface: A silly song about female astronauts is being made into a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: PO for a child's potty is a crossword staple; the title is two words, the second given by the end of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppola's 1979 Vietnam War movie is the film in question.

clue.text: Inventor brought up free of impertinence?

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: side is old slang for swagger or impertinence, so having no side means being free of it

explanation.surface: An inventor was raised without any cheekiness, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE is chiefly British slang for putting on airs; NO SIDE turned upward gives the American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb, is a famous inventor.

clue.text: Pilot was broadcast in London

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot was on the radio in London.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAISTOW is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition stands for a place located in the capital, which this East End district is.

clue.text: Access to the pit of modern computing?

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era of dates
IT, information technology, means computing

explanation.surface: It asks whether today's technology lets you into a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal tunnel giving entry to a mine.

clue.text: Gold weight compassing humbug's precursor on major road

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: compassing means surrounding, so the weight goes round the exclamation

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
Scrooge says 'Bah, humbug!', so the word before humbug is bah

explanation.surface: Precious metal and a heavy load surround a sweet on a big highway.
explanation.walkthrough: Humbug is also a British boiled sweet, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a major road.

clue.text: Pulse in the head

explanation.surface: A heartbeat felt inside one's skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A bean is a pulse (an edible seed) and is slang for the head.

clue.text: Be gentle with accomplished female reversing into the sun

indicators.note: into places the turned pieces inside the word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the sun

indicators.note: reversing turns the skilled word and the female abbreviation backwards together

parts.note: adept means accomplished or skilled

explanation.surface: A skilled woman drives backwards into the sunset, gently.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'reversing', turns both the skill word and the female letter together before they go into the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal something is to play it down, to treat it gently.

clue.text: Feel free to take advantage of being put out

parts.note: an invitation like 'do sit down' uses do to mean feel free to
to use something is to take advantage of it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to exploit a situation while feeling miffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do use the pool' is a polite way to say feel free to use it; 'put out' looks like annoyed, but means extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse a fire is to put it out by drenching it.

clue.text: Alice suffers discombobulation of the gut

indicators.note: being discombobulated is being thrown into confusion, so the name's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Alice is thrown into confusion by a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac means relating to the ileum, part of the small intestine.

clue.text: Unexpectedly dine with Tintin and Jehovah's Witness (of 3)

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as one of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Jehovah's Witness turns up surprisingly to eat with the boy reporter Tintin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jehovah's Witness' reads as one phrase, but 'Witness' is the definition; the S of 'Jehovah's' is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This apostle is traditionally the author of the Book of Revelation, the witness behind the visions of 3.

clue.text: Pet name for boy from Barcelona, perhaps

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone picks a pet name for a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet name' looks like one phrase, a nickname; it splits into an animal and a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is in Catalonia, so a person from there may be described as a Catalan.

clue.text: It adds flavour to antic

explanation.surface: A seasoning lends taste to a playful prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a pickled bud used for flavour, and also a playful antic or prank.

clue.text: Acts to restrict graduate headgear

indicators.note: to restrict is to hold in, so the performances enclose the graduate

parts.note: turns are acts or routines in a variety show
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Performers confine a university leaver's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbans are wound cloth head coverings, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: English verse tale about 3

indicators.note: about has the narrative wrapped round the two abbreviations

parts.note: a relation is an account or telling of a story

explanation.surface: An English poem tells a story about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places EV inside RELATION after its R; the definition is the answer to 3-down, the Greek name for this book.
explanation.definitionFit: The last book of the Bible is known both by this name and by its Greek title meaning an unveiling.

clue.text: Poles taking in country girl

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the poles go round the country

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
the USA is a country

explanation.surface: Polish immigrants welcome a country lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the compass points S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female given name, so it fits a clue asking simply for a girl.

clue.text: Growth of Tallis's music, say, after 50% cut

indicators.note: a half cut away means the back half of the word is removed

parts.note: Thomas Tallis wrote polyphonic music, interweaving several independent lines

explanation.surface: The output of a Tudor composer grows after half of it is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting the back half of POLYPHONIC removes HONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small growth, as on a mucous membrane.

clue.text: Drunk lost head and made a run

indicators.note: losing its head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: bladdered is British slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk lost his temper and ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: BLADDERED is British slang for very drunk; a run is a ladder in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights that have laddered have developed a run, a line of broken stitches.

clue.text: See 3
Unaware of nice mess in egg container

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the bird's home

parts.note: a nest holds a bird's eggs

indicators.note: making a mess of something throws it into disorder, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant of a nice mess finds themselves in an egg box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is the anagram signal, hiding in plain sight as a noun after 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a literary word for ignorant, not knowing.

clue.text: Love reversing gas guzzler around Tyneside etc

indicators.note: reversing turns the whole assembled piece backwards
around has the vehicle enclose the region

parts.note: an SUV, sport utility vehicle, is a fuel-hungry car
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Someone backs a big car around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' acts on the whole car-around-region assembly, not just the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman goddess of love.

clue.text: Compensation for ginger hair? Not initially

parts.note: red is the colour of ginger hair

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone seeks damages for being a redhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' drops the T of TRESS to leave RESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is compensation for a wrong or grievance.

clue.text: Second character in Arabian Nights disembowelled by Arabian warrior

indicators.note: disembowelled means the innards go, so a middle letter is removed

parts.note: Aladdin is a tale from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A secondary figure from the Arabian Nights is gutted by a desert fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disembowelled' removes one of the middle Ds of ALADDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Small girl on island

parts.note: Kerry is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A little girl lives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky island or reef.

clue.text: Property of Electra's instruction to Orestes?

explanation.surface: Something a Greek heroine owns is passed on to her brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Electra urged her brother Orestes to kill their mother, Clytemnestra: 'Do Ma in!'
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is an estate or territory one owns, a property.

clue.text: See 12
Time to question Labour

parts.note: to ask is to question

explanation.surface: It's time to interrogate the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' wears a capital to suggest the British party; it means work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work, labour.

clue.text: Dubious moment to go topless

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter is the first, so it goes

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A dubious moment to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious.

clue.text: "Follow My Leader" enters the language

indicators.note: enters means going inside the word for following

parts.note: to tail is to follow

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A children's game makes its way into the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow My Leader' is a children's game, but splits into three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a language spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Stroke bit of hair

explanation.surface: Stroking a strand of someone's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is a stroke of a whip, and an eyelash, a bit of hair.

clue.text: Board with quiet sprite

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an elf is a sprite

explanation.surface: A plank alongside a silent fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a flat board fixed to a wall for holding things.

clue.text: Arrangement of endless Costa Rican numbers

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered
endless means the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of songs from Costa Rica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts COSTA to COST; with RICAN that is rearranged. 'numbers' looks like songs but means things that numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs that dull the senses, things that numb.
